receiver: the user approving the architecture at the design sign-off, and whoever builds the tool and its tests to it
use: approving how the tool is put together and checked, and building the tool and its tests to what it says

questions.question: The architecture's Test section is to link the project's rules for how each kind of part (here, Python code) and the user stories are checked, but no file given for this run, the steering, the README or the plan's files, names such rules. Where are they: a file to link, or none, in which case the architecture's Test section itself says how this tool's code and stories are checked?
questions.recommended: If the project has no such rules, let the architecture's Test section say it, in the line for what this product's checks need: the code checked by tests with Python's own unittest, each story by running the tool on a temporary test folder holding every case, all run by one command, as that meets AC11 with nothing to install beyond Python.

answers.answer: Answer to your question on the project's rules for checks (F-1, B-5): a CCS question, and the CCS (.rn/20261026-organize-downloads/calls/0006-ccs.json) now holds it as a choice; read it anew. The repository holds no such rules, so take your recommendation: the architecture's Test section says the project has none and itself gives what this tool's checks need, the code checked by tests with Python's own unittest and each user story by running the tool on a temporary test folder holding every case, all run by one command.

questions.question: The architecture's Logical view is to be one figure in an SVG file beside the document, shown in it as an image, but the CCS names only organize-downloads/docs/architecture.md as the work, so the figure's file cannot be written in this run. May an SVG file beside the architecture, such as organize-downloads/docs/architecture.svg, be added to the work?
questions.recommended: Add it to the CCS as a focal entity of the same kind as the architecture's own, {"path": "organize-downloads/docs/architecture.svg"}, as the checklist's template asks the figure to be drawn by hand in an SVG beside the document, and without it the reader cannot see how the components achieve each user story.

answers.answer: Answer to your question on the figure (F-1, B-3): yes. The CCS (.rn/20261026-organize-downloads/calls/0006-ccs.json) now holds organize-downloads/docs/architecture.svg as a path of this work beside organize-downloads/docs/architecture.md, with a choice saying it is the Logical view's figure; read the CCS anew.

back.did: I followed each story through the arrows and lines. List: Command line asks Planner, Planner reads the folder, Command line prints. Move: the same plan goes to the Mover, which moves files and adds each move through the Record keeper. Undo: Command line asks the Undoer, which reads the last move through the Record keeper and moves files back. Help: Command line prints. All four are achieved, and the order of the arrows is in lines 39-42. I then tested the Mover's choice in a mktemp -d folder with python3 -I (Python 3.14.4). os.link('a','b') onto an existing b raised FileExistsError and left both files unchanged. os.rename('a','b') replaced b. The why at lines 55-57 is therefore true.
back.lacking: The first story, and the README, let the user work on 'another folder' (README lines 90-95: '--move ~/Desktop'). The Mover moves only by making a hard link, and gives no other way. A builder or approver would ask at once what happens on a folder whose drive cannot make hard links, such as a USB stick formatted FAT or exFAT, or some network shares. There os.link fails for every file, so no run of arrows achieves the move story there. The lines do not say whether the tool refuses such a folder, reports each file as staying (and with what reason), or falls back to some other kind of move. Without this I cannot approve the choice knowing what it costs the user, and a builder would have to guess. Less important: to say 'stays, Documents/budget.xlsx already exists', the Planner must also read the names inside the kinds' folders. The figure's 'reads the names of its files' and the lines leave that for the reader to work out.

chosen.chosen: The Mover moves a file by a hard link to its new name and then removing the old name, never by a rename.
chosen.why: A rename replaces a file that took the name after the Planner looked, while a hard link to a taken name fails and leaves both files, as checked with os.link and os.rename on a temporary folder, so the principle of never overwriting holds.

chosen.chosen: The Mover has each move and each kind's folder added to the record as soon as it is made, the first of these in a run starting the folder's record anew.
chosen.why: A run stopped half way can still be undone, and a run that moves nothing leaves the last move's record for --undo, as the README's 'the last --move on that folder' and G1's 'the last run that moved files' ask.

chosen.chosen: One record per folder, a JSON Lines file named by a hash of the folder's full path and holding that path, in organize-downloads/ under the place AC12 names.
chosen.why: A move in one folder never replaces another's record, a hash is always short enough for a file name, and a line written per move survives a run stopped half way.

chosen.chosen: Tests under organize-downloads/tests, one test_<component>.py per component and test_stories.py for the stories, run by python3 -m unittest discover organize-downloads/tests.
chosen.why: unittest's discover finds files named test_*.py with no setup, which gives the one command AC11 asks with nothing to install.
